answer: A bond is refunded only after 15 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. The velvet counter is kept in tide and cipher exposes each reset. An attacker therefore has to keep each duplicate self continuously active for 15 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. Each duplicate costs another 126 dollars in locked collateral and another 1 days of waiting. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
